entries.clue: Theatrical maiden wearing hat (4)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the hat is worn around the maiden, so CAP goes outside M

blocks.note: m = maiden, a cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over with no runs

annotation.surface: A young woman in a hat on the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatrical maiden' reads as an actress; 'Theatrical' stands alone as the definition, in its sense of showy and exaggerated.
annotation.definitionFit: Camp means exaggerated and affected in manner, i.e. theatrical.

entries.clue: Leader beginning to wear underskirts and bloomers (8)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of 'wear' is its first letter, W

annotation.surface: Someone in charge putting on petticoats and old-fashioned knickers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' reads as underwear alongside 'underskirts', but here it means things that bloom: flowers.
annotation.definitionFit: Cowslips are yellow spring wild flowers, so they are bloomers.

entries.clue: Naked orangeman dancing for Michael O'Neill? (7)

indicatorNotes.Naked: a naked word is stripped of its outer letters
indicatorNotes.dancing: the letters move about into a new order

blocks.note: ORANGEMAN without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A nude Orangeman — a member of the Protestant Orange Order in Northern Ireland — dancing in honour of a famous Northern Irishman.
annotation.walkthrough: Michael O'Neill managed the Northern Ireland football team, which ties in with the Orangeman; the question mark marks him as one example of a manager.
annotation.definitionFit: Michael O'Neill is a football manager, so he is an example of the answer.

entries.clue: Program run to attract trainee (10)

blocks.note: an app is a computer program
r = run, as on a cricket scorecard

annotation.surface: A software scheme set up to bring in new recruits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb meaning operate the program; it is only the letter R.
annotation.definitionFit: An apprentice is someone learning a trade, a trainee.

entries.clue: Train carrying post around assembly (10)

indicatorNotes.around: MAIL is turned around to LIAM

blocks.note: to parent a child is to raise and train it

annotation.surface: A railway train loaded with letters and parcels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Train' reads as the railway kind carrying the post; it is a verb meaning bring up, as a parent does a child.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the elected body that meets to make a nation's laws is its assembly.

entries.clue: Fascinated emerging from contraption (4)

indicatorNotes.emerging from: the answer comes out of the word that follows

annotation.surface: Someone spellbound as they climb out of a strange machine.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer sits in the middle of a single word, which makes it easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: Rapt means completely absorbed, fascinated.

entries.clue: State of tipsy tailor on ranch (5,8)

indicatorNotes.tipsy: a tipsy tailor's letters stagger out of order

annotation.surface: A drunken tailor working on a cattle ranch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State of' seems to describe the tailor's condition; 'State' is the definition, a US state.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the fifty US states, on the Atlantic coast south of Virginia.

entries.clue: Second insurance worker touring Thailand (7)

indicatorNotes.touring: the worker goes round Thailand, so T sits inside INS ANT

blocks.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
the ant is the standard worker

annotation.surface: An insurance employee on a trip round Thailand for a second time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second insurance worker' reads as a second employee; 'Second' is the definition, a moment of time.
annotation.definitionFit: Just a second means just an instant: both are a very short time.

entries.clue: The Spanish duke's established to be the most senior (6)

blocks.note: D = duke; the 's that follows is 'is'
est. = established, as on shop signs

annotation.surface: A Spanish duke has been confirmed as the senior figure.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in duke's does nothing but link; EST is the usual abbreviation for 'established' on signs and labels.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: among siblings, the first-born is the most senior in age.

entries.clue: Victor gets award for Northumbrian castle (7)

indicatorNotes.for: the award stands in place of the Northumbrian letters

blocks.note: Northumberland is in the North East, NE
DSO = Distinguished Service Order, a military award

annotation.surface: A winner is honoured with a prize for a castle in Northumberland.
annotation.walkthrough: WINNER swaps its NE for DSO. 'Northumbrian castle' reads as one phrase, but Windsor Castle is in Berkshire, west of London; the castle is the definition alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the royal family's Berkshire residence, the oldest occupied castle in the world.

entries.clue: Sneakiest cost involved to obtain travel passes (6,7)

annotation.surface: A sly hidden charge you have to pay to get your commuter passes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a complaint about hidden fees, a fitting picture for season tickets.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: commuters buy these to ride as often as they like for a month or a year.

entries.clue: Went over with a Yankee editor (7)

blocks.note: a = per, as in 'once a day'

annotation.surface: An American editor checked through something with someone.
annotation.walkthrough: The tiny word 'a' gives PER: 'ten pounds a head' means ten pounds per head.
annotation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read over carefully, so perused means went over.

entries.clue: What director of Taxi may do in backwoods' location (3,5)

blocks.clueFragment: What director of Taxi may do
blocks.note: whoever directs a taxi firm might log (record) a cab

annotation.surface: A film-maker's routine, set somewhere out in the wilds.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics make Taxi look like the title of a show; read it as an ordinary taxi and its dispatcher would 'log cab in'.
annotation.definitionFit: A log cabin is the typical dwelling found in the backwoods.

entries.clue: On board facilities for leaders (5)

blocks.note: sailors' word for a ship's toilets
people in charge, as of schools or departments

annotation.surface: Company directors get special amenities in the boardroom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' reads as the company board, but it means aboard ship, where the lavatories are called the heads.
annotation.definitionFit: Sailors call a ship's toilets the heads, and a head is a leader.

entries.clue: A local group overseeing education is illiterate (10)

indicatorNotes.overseeing: in a down clue, what oversees something sits above it

blocks.note: 'un is how a local dialect speaker might say 'one', i.e. a
a school is a group, of fish or of painters

annotation.surface: A council body in charge of schools turns out not to be able to read.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A local group' reads as a council committee; 'local' only marks dialect for 'a', as in 'a good 'un'.
annotation.definitionFit: Unschooled means without education, so unable to read or write.

entries.clue: Presumably star in ballet and opera? (10,4)

annotation.definition: Presumably star in ballet and opera?

blocks.note: a star on stage is, presumably, doing what stars do: appearing before an audience
the surface reads this as where the star works; the setter means the genres themselves, the name for such stage arts

annotation.surface: A leading dancer or singer taking the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a category, but the clue reads it as a verb phrase: what a star does in ballet and opera is perform in arts. 'Presumably' and the question mark flag the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: The phrase is read two ways: the umbrella term for ballet and opera, and a description of what their star does.

entries.clue: India's very happy to leave England cut off (8)

indicatorNotes.to leave: England departs from the word for happy, so its E is dropped

blocks.note: India is I in the radio alphabet; the 's that follows is 'is'

annotation.surface: India is delighted to be done with England.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's just joins India to the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a village cut off by floods is left alone, apart from everywhere else.

entries.clue: Lots may be wrapped up in these culinary treats (7,7)

annotation.definition: Lots may be wrapped up in these culinary treats

blocks.note: the surface means 'plenty can be packed'; the setter means one's lot, one's destiny, folded up inside
the crisp biscuits served after a Chinese restaurant meal

annotation.surface: Plenty of goodies can come gift-wrapped as tasty snacks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lots' reads as 'a great many', but a lot is one's fate or fortune, and those are what fortune cookies wrap up.
annotation.definitionFit: Fortune cookies are crisp sweet biscuits with a printed fortune folded inside.

entries.clue: Longing to forget partners' source of pain (7)

indicatorNotes.to forget: NOSTALGIA forgets the letters N and S

blocks.note: nostalgia is a longing for the past
in bridge North and South are partners, N and S

annotation.surface: Pining for lost lovers is what really hurts.
annotation.walkthrough: Bridge partners sit opposite each other: North with South, East with West.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical term for earache, so the ear is where the pain comes from; the definition names that source loosely.

entries.clue: Fashionable communist collects one piece of music (7)

indicatorNotes.collects: TROT collects I, holding it inside

annotation.surface: A trendy leftist picks up a musical score.
annotation.walkthrough: A Trot is a follower of Trotsky, a common crossword shorthand for any hard-left communist.
annotation.definitionFit: An introit is a piece of music sung at the start of a church service.

entries.clue: Note medic starts to investigate blood in vein (6)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the starts of the next two words

blocks.note: mi is a note in do-re-mi
first letters of Investigate and Blood

annotation.surface: A doctor makes a note to check for blood in a vein.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'vein' a blood vessel; it is the main vein of a leaf.
annotation.definitionFit: The midrib is the central vein running down a leaf.

entries.clue: Type of investment account for Ishmael's half-brother (5)

blocks.note: an ISA (Individual Savings Account) is a British tax-free savings and investment account

annotation.surface: Opening a savings account on behalf of a biblical figure.
annotation.walkthrough: In Genesis Abraham fathered Ishmael by Hagar and Isaac by Sarah, making them half-brothers.
annotation.definitionFit: Isaac and Ishmael were both sons of Abraham by different mothers.

entries.clue: Community of former independent island returns (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Community' is used as a modifier, as in 'community values', matching the adjective SOCIETAL

indicatorNotes.returns: the whole string goes back the other way

blocks.note: late = former, as in 'the late chairman'

annotation.surface: A once self-governing island people make a comeback.
annotation.walkthrough: LATE + I + COS is built first, then the whole reads backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Societal means relating to society, the community as a whole.

entries.clue: Regularly bans visas for approximately 60% of the world’s population (4)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

annotation.surface: A country routinely refuses entry permits to most of humanity.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a fact rather than a synonym: about three in five people live in Asia.
annotation.definitionFit: Asia is home to roughly 60% of the world's people.

entries.clue: Leader of Russian fliers feels remorse (7)

indicatorNotes.Leader of: the leader of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: The head of a Russian air squadron is sorry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fliers' suggests pilots next to 'Leader of Russian'; they are birds.
annotation.definitionFit: To regret something is to feel remorse about it.

entries.clue: Some bleak outcomes emerge (4,3)

indicatorNotes.Some: some of the letters that follow make the answer

annotation.surface: Bad results are coming to light.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is the very thing the surface describes: bleak outcomes leaking out.
annotation.definitionFit: When news leaks out it emerges, becomes known.

entries.clue: Players' money belts (5,5)

blocks.note: brass is British slang for money

annotation.surface: Money belts belonging to sportsmen or actors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Players' reads as footballers or actors; it means musicians. Brass is old northern English slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: ensembles of cornet, horn and tuba players, a fixture of northern English towns.

entries.clue: Boss backing out of room (4)

indicatorNotes.backing out of: the back of the word, its last letter, goes out of it

annotation.surface: The boss retreats out of the room in reverse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not an employer but a raised knob or stud, as on a shield. 'Backing' tempts a reversal, but nothing is turned round: the back letter goes out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the metalwork sense: a raised ornamental knob, like those on a shield or a leather belt.
